brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: A hex-acc-keyhole-x3 runs up the back face (slot 1) of all three cells. It hangs on screws already in the wall. The wall's and screws' load capacity was not checked.

9 hex-acc-hook plates (18 hooks) on slots 3, 4 and 5 of levels 0, 1 and 2, all facing away from the wall. Staged with 2 cable coils and a roll of gaffer tape. The configurator offers no hand-tool props that hang on hooks, so none are shown. How much weight the printed hooks can hold depends on the material and was not checked.

requirements.requirement: A tool rack form (modest, stable build)
requirements.evidence: 27 parts. The joints are bolted (lockJoints). check_build: no rule errors, mesh clash clear. It lists 6 faces that could take a cap: an information note, not an error.

finish.summary: I built the rack as a column of three full hex cells stacked at (0,0), levels 0 to 2. One three-storey keyhole hanger runs up the back face (slot 1) so the rack hangs on screws already in the wall. Nine hook plates fill the front three faces of each storey (slots 3, 4 and 5); each plate carries two hooks, so there are 18 hooks in all. The house rules ran: capOpenFaces added no caps, and check_build still lists 6 faces that could take a cap. This is an information note, not an error. lockJoints bolted the joints. For staging I hung a cable coil on the middle storey's front hook. On the top storey I hung a roll of gaffer tape on one angled face and another cable coil on the other. A tape roll on the bottom hook was refused because it would hang through the bench. In my one look from the back, the second cable coil was hidden behind the build. check_build passes with no rule errors, no prop warnings, and the mesh check reads clear. The configurator does not check how much weight it can hold.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
